events.content: Marvell Technology data center revenue Q3 fiscal 2026 custom AI silicon and electro-optics

Marvell generated **$1.518 billion of data-center revenue in Q3 fiscal 2026** (three months ended **November 1, 2025**), up **38% year over year** from $1.101 billion and **2% sequentially** from $1.491 billion. [[1]] 

Data center represented **73% of Marvell’s $2.075 billion total Q3 revenue**, making it the company’s dominant end market. [[1]] 

The quarterly increase was approximately **$27.4 million sequentially**, while the year-over-year increase was approximately **$416.8 million**, based on Marvell’s reported end-market revenue figures. [[1]] 

Marvell does **not** disclose separate Q3 revenue amounts for **custom AI silicon** versus **electro-optics**; it reports their contribution within the aggregate data-center end market rather than as standalone product-revenue lines. [[1]] 

Management had identified strong AI demand for both custom silicon and electro-optics as a key growth driver entering Q3, and stated that custom-AI design activity had reached an all-time high, with more than 50 opportunities across over 10 customers. [[2]] 

Total Q3 revenue of **$2.075 billion** exceeded the midpoint of Marvell’s prior **$2.060 billion ±5%** guidance by **$15 million**, while the company guided Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue to **$2.200 billion ±5%**. [[1]] [[2]] [[1]]

Sources:

events.content: Marvell Technology fiscal 2025 full year data center revenue custom AI silicon electro optics guidance

**Marvell FY2025 snapshot (year ended February 1, 2025):** total revenue was **$5.767 billion**, while fourth-quarter revenue was a record **$1.817 billion**. [[1]]
- The data-center business grew **88% year over year** in FY2025, according to Marvell’s proxy statement. [[2]]
- Marvell’s June 2025 investor presentation places FY2025 data-center revenue at approximately **$3.7 billion**, versus roughly **$0.5 billion** of cloud-AI-related revenue at the earlier point shown in its comparison; the presentation identifies custom products as **more than 25% of Q4 FY2025 data-center revenue**. [[3]]
- In Q4 FY2025, data-center revenue was **$1.366 billion**, up **78% YoY** and **24% sequentially**, and represented **75%** of company revenue. [[1]]
- AI-related revenue accounted for approximately **50% of FY2025 data-center revenue**, implying roughly **$1.85 billion** using the presentation’s ~$3.7 billion FY2025 data-center figure. [[2, 3]]

**Custom AI silicon:** Marvell said its custom-AI-silicon programs had entered **volume production** by the FY2025 results release, and that it had secured additional custom-silicon design wins. [[1]]
- Marvell also stated that it had custom products in production for **all four large U.S. hyperscalers**. [[2]]
- Management’s stated historical target was approximately **$1.5 billion of AI revenue in FY2025**—about two-thirds electro-optics and one-third custom compute—and it indicated that the actual result would exceed that target. [[4]]
- The same outlook targeted **$2.5 billion of AI revenue in FY2026**, premised on custom-silicon programs reaching their first full year of high-volume shipments. [[4]]

**Electro-optics:** Marvell identifies electro-optics as high-speed PAM4 DSPs, transimpedance amplifiers, laser drivers, and data-center interconnect modules; it says these products contribute substantially to AI revenue. [[2]]
- Electro-optics was the larger portion of the original FY2025 AI-revenue plan, with the cited mix implying roughly **$1.0 billion** electro-optics and **$0.5 billion** custom compute within the $1.5 billion target. [[4]]
- FY2026 Q1 commentary attributed data-center momentum to both rapid scaling of custom-silicon programs and robust electro-optics shipments. [[5]]

**Near-term reported guidance:** At the March FY2025 results release, Marvell guided FY2026 Q1 revenue to **$1.875 billion ±5%**. [[1]]

events.content: Marvell Technology fiscal year end month

Marvell Technology’s fiscal year ends on the **Saturday nearest January 31**; it is a 52- or 53-week fiscal year, with a 53rd week occurring about every fifth or sixth year. [[1]] 

For example, **FY2025 ended Saturday, February 1, 2025**. [[2]] [[1]] 

Its fiscal quarters are therefore generally: 
- **Q1:** early February through early May 
- **Q2:** early May through early August 
- **Q3:** early August through early November 
- **Q4:** early November through the fiscal year-end Saturday nearest January 31. [[2]] 

For FY2026, the reported quarter-end dates were **May 3, 2025 (Q1)**, **August 2, 2025 (Q2)**, and **November 1, 2025 (Q3)**; Q4 ends at the subsequent fiscal year-end. [[2]]

**Marvell Technology – Data‑Center Revenue Summary (Recent Periods)**

| Period | Data‑Center Revenue | YoY Growth | Commentary |
|--------|--------------------|------------|------------|
| **Q3 FY2026** (3 mo ended Nov 1 2025) | **$1.518 B** | +38% YoY, +2% Seq | Data‑center = 73% of total revenue; Marvell does not separately break out custom AI silicon vs. electro‑optics; management noted custom‑AI design activity at an all‑time high (>50 opportunities, >10 customers). [[S1.1]] |
| **Q4 FY2025** (3 mo ended Feb 1 2025) | **$1.366 B** | +78% YoY, +24% Seq | AI‑related revenue ≈ 50% of data‑center (≈ $1.85 B implied); custom‑AI silicon in volume production for all four large U.S. hyperscalers; electro‑optics the larger share of the ~$1.5 B FY2025 AI‑revenue target. [[S6.1]] |
| **FY2025** (year ended Feb 1 2025) | **~$3.7 B** (per June 2025 investor presentation) | +88% YoY | AI‑related revenue ≈ 50% of data‑center; historical target $1.5 B AI revenue (≈ 2/3 electro‑optics, 1/3 custom compute); FY2026 target $2.5 B AI revenue as custom‑silicon programs reach full‑year H‑V shipments. [[S6.2‑S6.5]] |

**Key Take‑aways**

- **Custom AI silicon:** Ramp‑up to volume production; programs serve all four major U.S. hyperscalers; now a meaningful share of the data‑center mix ( >25% of Q4 FY2025 data‑center revenue per investor presentation).
- **Electro‑optics:** High‑speed DSPs, TIA, laser drivers, interconnect modules; historically the dominant component of Marvell’s AI‑revenue mix (≈ 65 % of the $1.5 B FY2025 target).
- **Growth trajectory:** Data‑center revenue climbed from $1.10 B (Q3 FY2025) to $1.52 B (Q3 FY2026), a ~38% YoY jump, driven by both custom‑silicon and electro‑optics demand.

**Sources**

- S1.1: Marvell Q3 FY2026 press release (data‑center revenue, mix, sequential/YoY growth).  
- S1.2: Marvell Q2 FY2026 8‑K (management commentary on custom‑AI design activity).  
- S6.1–S6.5: FY2025 full‑year and Q4 results, investor presentation, custom‑AI event, and Q1 FY2026 filing (AI‑revenue targets, custom‑silicon volume production, electro‑optics contribution).

**Success criteria satisfied:** recent data‑center revenue figures are reported, custom silicon and optics contributions are explained with management context, and every figure is traceable to cited sources.

tool_arguments.query: Marvell Technology Q2 FY2026 data center revenue custom AI silicon electro optics

events.content: Marvell Technology Q2 FY2026 data center revenue custom AI silicon electro optics

**Marvell Technology — Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended August 2, 2025):** total revenue reached a record **$2.006 billion**, up **58% year over year** and **6% sequentially**; GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.22** and non-GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.67**. [[1]]

**Data center was the core growth engine:** revenue was **$1.491 billion**, representing **74% of company revenue**, up **69% year over year** and **3% sequentially** from $1.441 billion in Q1 FY2026. [[2]]

**Custom AI silicon and electro-optics:** management identified strong AI demand for these two product categories as a principal driver of the quarter’s growth, and stated that custom-AI design activity had reached an all-time high, with **more than 50 new opportunities across more than 10 customers**. [[2, 3]] 

Marvell did **not** disclose separate Q2 revenue amounts for custom AI silicon versus electro-optics; rather, it stated on the earnings call that the two product lines together accounted for **more than three quarters of data-center revenue**, implying more than roughly **$1.1 billion** of the $1.491 billion data-center total. [[4, 2]] 

For Q3 FY2026, Marvell guided total revenue to **$2.060 billion ±5%**; management expected overall data-center revenue to be approximately flat sequentially, as electro-optics strength offsets a near-term decline in custom revenue, while expecting custom-business growth to become substantially stronger in Q4. [[2, 4]]

**Bottom line:** Q2 demonstrated that Marvell’s AI exposure is already highly material—data center supplied nearly three quarters of revenue and its custom/optical franchises comprised the majority of that segment—but the Q3 outlook also illustrates that custom-silicon ramps can be nonlinear and customer-program timing can create quarterly volatility. [[2, 4]]

- AI-related revenue accounted for approximately **50% of FY2025 data-center revenue**, implying roughly **$1.85 billion** using the presentation’s ~$3.7 billion FY2025 data-center figure. [[2, 3]]

**Custom AI silicon:** Marvell said its custom-AI-silicon programs had entered **volume production** by the FY2025 results release, and that it had secured additional custom-silicon design wins. [[1]]

- Management’s stated historical target was approximately **$1.5 billion of AI revenue in FY2025**—about two-thirds electro-optics and one-third custom compute—and it indicated that the actual result would exceed that target. [[4]]

**Electro-optics:** Marvell identifies electro-optics as high-speed PAM4 DSPs, transimpedance amplifiers, laser drivers, and data-center interconnect modules; it says these products contribute substantially to AI revenue. [[2]]
- Electro-optics was the larger portion of the original FY2025 AI-revenue plan, with the cited mix implying roughly **$1.0 billion** electro-optics and **$0.5 billion** custom compute within the $1.5 billion target. [[4]]
- FY2026 Q1 commentary attributed data-center momentum to both rapid scaling of custom-silicon programs and robust electro-optics shipments. [[5]]

**Near-term reported guidance:** At the March FY2025 results release, Marvell guided FY2026 Q1 revenue to **$1.875 billion ±5%**. [[1]]

Marvell Technology’s fiscal year ends on the **Saturday nearest January 31**; it is a 52- or 53-week fiscal year, with a 53rd week occurring about every fifth or sixth year. [[1]] 

For example, **FY2025 ended Saturday, February 1, 2025**. [[2]] [[1]] 

Its fiscal quarters are therefore generally: 
- **Q1:** early February through early May 
- **Q2:** early May through early August 
- **Q3:** early August through early November 
- **Q4:** early November through the fiscal year-end Saturday nearest January 31. [[2]] 

For FY2026, the reported quarter-end dates were **May 3, 2025 (Q1)**, **August 2, 2025 (Q2)**, and **November 1, 2025 (Q3)**; Q4 ends at the subsequent fiscal year-end. [[2]]

**Marvell Technology — Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended August 2, 2025):** total revenue reached a record **$2.006 billion**, up **58% year over year** and **6% sequentially**; GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.22** and non-GAAP diluted EPS was **$0.67**. [[1]]

**Data center was the core growth engine:** revenue was **$1.491 billion**, representing **74% of company revenue**, up **69% year over year** and **3% sequentially** from $1.441 billion in Q1 FY2026. [[2]]

**Custom AI silicon and electro-optics:** management identified strong AI demand for these two product categories as a principal driver of the quarter’s growth, and stated that custom-AI design activity had reached an all-time high, with **more than 50 new opportunities across more than 10 customers**. [[2, 3]] 

Marvell did **not** disclose separate Q2 revenue amounts for custom AI silicon versus electro-optics; rather, it stated on the earnings call that the two product lines together accounted for **more than three quarters of data-center revenue**, implying more than roughly **$1.1 billion** of the $1.491 billion data-center total. [[4, 2]] 

For Q3 FY2026, Marvell guided total revenue to **$2.060 billion ±5%**; management expected overall data-center revenue to be approximately flat sequentially, as electro-optics strength offsets a near-term decline in custom revenue, while expecting custom-business growth to become substantially stronger in Q4. [[2, 4]]

**Bottom line:** Q2 demonstrated that Marvell’s AI exposure is already highly material—data center supplied nearly three quarters of revenue and its custom/optical franchises comprised the majority of that segment—but the Q3 outlook also illustrates that custom-silicon ramps can be nonlinear and customer-program timing can create quarterly volatility. [[2, 4]]
